Subject-Guidelines for Selection and Registration of NPTEL Course(s) 
 
All students are hereby notified that the process of selection and registration of NPTEL 
course(s) shall be undertaken strictly in accordance with the guidelines outlined below. Students are 
required to ensure full compliance with these instructions. 
The University must have circulate a Google Form for submission of student preferences f or NPTEL 
course(s). Students must ensure that their course selection is final prior to submission of the 
preference form. Before filling the preference form, students shall visit the official NPTEL portal at  
https://swayam.gov.in/nc_details/NPTEL and search for the intended course(s). 
Students shall carefully verify and record the Course Start Date, End Date, and Examination Date of 
each selected course. 
In accordance with NPTEL regulations, a student is permitted to appear in a maximum of TWO 
NPTEL examinations on a single day. Students must ensure that their selected course(s) comply with 
this restriction. 
Registration for NPTEL course(s) must be completed exclusively using the official University email 
ID (@nsut.ac.in). Registrations made through personal or non-official email IDs shall not be 
considered valid. 
NOTE- The responsibility for correct course selection, verification of examination schedules, and 
adherence to all NPTEL and University guidelines rests solely with the student. 
Students are advised to adhere strictly to the above instructions to avoid any inconvenience at later 
stages. 
 
NPTEL Co-ordinator

NOTICE 
 
Call for Student Participation in Innovation & Entrepreneurship Projects 
Centre of Excellence in Hydroponics 
 
The Centre of Excellence in Hydroponics invites motivated and innovative students to participate in a 
series of entrepreneurship-driven, technology-enabled projects currently under development. These 
projects aim to foster skill development, hands-on research, and start-up incubation opportunities in 
the domains of sustainable agriculture, smart farming, renewable energy, and urban environmental 
solutions. 
Students from all branches are encouraged to apply. 
Benefits: 
• Certificates and letters of contribution for active participants 
• Hands-on experience with advanced technologies 
• Opportunity to co-develop prototypes and publications 
• Pathways to start-up incubation and commercialization 
Who Can Apply: 
• Students from B. Tech, M. Tech, BBA, MBA, B Design, M.Sc., PhD. 
• Both individual and team-based participation permitted 
How to Apply: 
Interested students may register by filling out the participation form accessible through the following 
link: 
https://forms.gle/ajq4y7dCHPFLXReq9 
Last Date for Application: 17th December 2025 
Students with their own innovative ideas related to agriculture, environment, renewable energy, 
hydroponics, AI/ML, biotechnology, product design, or sustainability are strongly encouraged to 
propose and pursue them under the Centre’s mentorship. The Centr e welcomes fresh concepts and 
will provide full support for idea development, prototype building, and potential incubation. 
Projects Available for Participation: 
1. IoT-Based Smart Hydroponic Controllers  Creation of automated nutrient dosing, pH/EC 
monitoring, and environmental regulation systems. Students will work with sensors, 
microcontrollers, app integration, and industrial IoT applications. 
2. AI-Based Plant Health Monitoring Softwar e Development of AI/ML models for plant stress 
detection using RGB and hyperspectral imaging. Students will contribute to dataset creation, 
model building, and development of mobile/desktop applications for real -time plant 
diagnostics. 
3. Biochar Production Units Design of small-scale biochar systems and development of biochar-
based products aimed at soil improvement, carbon sequestration, and eco-friendly packaging. 
4. Plant-Based Microbial Fuel Cells (PMFCs) Research on renewable electricity generation from 
plant–microbe systems. Students will work on improving power output, system integration, 
and prototype development, including PMFC-integrated hydroponic towers. 
5. Designer & Modular Hydroponic Setups  Development of aesthetic and space -efficient 
hydroponic systems for urban households, schools, offices, and restaurants. Students will gain 
experience in design prototyping, fabrication, modular integration, and market -oriented 
product development. 
6. Aquaponics Systems Development of compact and decorative aquaponics units integrating 
ornamental fish and edible crops, along with IoT-based water quality monitoring. 
7. Terrace & Balcony Gardening Kits  Designing ready -to-use urban gardening kits with 
lightweight grow beds, substrates, and irrigation systems. Suitable for entrepreneurship in 
urban farming solutions. 
8. Specialized LED Grow Lights  Development of energy -efficient, crop -specific LED lighting 
systems for indoor cultivation. Students will learn about lighting technology, plant physiology, 
and product design. 
9. Medicinal Plants through Hydroponics Hydroponic cultivation of high-value medicinal herbs 
for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications, including metabolite profiling and value -
added product development. 
10. Customized Hydroponic Nutrient Media  Standardization and packaging of crop -specific 
nutrient formulations for commercial use, aligned with ongoing optimization research on 
secondary metabolites. 
11. Hydroponic Air Purification Towers  Development of plant -based air purification systems 
integrating mist scrubbers and IoT-enabled air quality monitoring. 
 
 
Dr. Akhilesh Dubey 
Coordinator 
Centre of Excellence in Hydroponics
